developer_request: There is an old draft PR with useful account behavior, but it is far behind the current release branch. Keep the useful intent and rebuild only what is still missing on the current baseline.
known_facts: The historical PR contains unique behavior worth preserving but is too stale to merge safely.
Current code may already implement part of the old PR's intended behavior.
Historical UI, release documents, tests, and architecture assumptions may no longer be valid.
The desired outcome is behavioral parity for selected capabilities on the current baseline, not preservation of old commits.
expected_first_moves: establish the current release branch as implementation baseline
extract intended behaviors and security properties from the old PR independently of its code shape
compare each intended behavior with current implementation and tests
implement only missing behavior using current primitives and current quality gates
must_preserve: unique user-visible and security-relevant intent from the historical work
current release architecture and current test/release gates unless explicitly changed
must_not: merge or rebase a deeply stale PR wholesale merely to preserve its commits
copy stale release/status documents or superseded UI structure into current code
assume every file changed historically still represents missing behavior
equate successful merge with deployment or production readiness
lessons: Feature work needs a historical-intent salvage pattern for stale PRs and abandoned branches.
Behavior, invariants, and tests are the reusable assets; old implementation structure is only evidence.
Current baseline must dominate stale implementation while still preserving valid intent.
